## Claims
- [computed] Accepted task `research-attempt-research-plan-task-124-1` gives, for \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,2,4)\), quotient free ranks \(1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8,9,\ldots,24\), respectively; every torsion-invariant-factor list is empty. Hence \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6\). [accepted task research-attempt-research-plan-task-124-1]
- [source-backed] The two Theorem 5.4 families are indexed by \(\{s_\mu: i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 14-21; source-6, lines 24-33]
- [proved] Here \(a=b=2\), and the accepted generating families are
  \[
  \{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},\qquad
  \{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}.
  \]
  Each has six elements and generates \(J\). Its image therefore surjects \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z^6\). By the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, each image is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis; thus no proper subfamily generates \(J\).
- [proved] The requested \(c=4\) minimality corollary is established: both displayed six-element families are minimal generating sets of \(J\).

## Strategy
Extract task 124’s degreewise Smith data, sum the nonzero free ranks, and apply accepted generation plus indexed-family Nakayama.
